description: Per-variation costume material-pattern table: eight arrays of exported material/parent-material FNames that UGameCharacterMaterialController hides or shows according to a zero-based pattern index.

ID.simple: Row key referenced by CharacterVariation.Id_CharacterMaterial; several variations can share one material row.
ID.technical: FName row property exported as ID (ImportKeyField=Id). When the optional Row argument is null, SetMaterialPattern resolves the owner's cached CharacterRow and VariationIndex to a CharacterVariation row in CharacterVariationDataTables (DTM +0x400), rejects a None Id_CharacterMaterial, then searches CharacterMaterialDataTables (DTM +0x490) and uses the first matching table's row. A non-null Row argument bypasses that owner/variation chain. Every character caller in the reconstructed source passes null; the shikigami call with a null pointer belongs to the separate ShikigamiMaterial controller and table.

MaterialName_P1.technical: TArray<FName>; pattern 0 selects it. The parameter is int32, but the reconstructed retail body compares it as a float against 0 and 7, so only 0 through 7 proceed. Eight entries are sorted by bShow, applying every non-selected array with bShow=false and then the selected array with bShow=true. Each non-None name is an exact FName lookup in OutlineRimParameters, whose key is the parent-material name of a dynamic material harvested by Initialize; the matched material index is shown or hidden on every LOD when the mesh is a USkinnedMeshComponent. Unmatched names, None entries, and failed row/pattern checks produce no section toggle. A successful call stores the pattern in AppliedPattern.

MaterialName_P2.technical: TArray<FName>; switch case 1 selects it, and the hide-first/show-selected pass hides it for every other valid pattern. Array position does not encode a material slot: each non-None name is matched by exact FName against the harvested parent-material map described on P1. Exported arrays have six fixed slots with 'None' padding; CP_050_00, for example, contains MI_CP_050_00_Hair_P2 here.

MaterialName_P3.technical: TArray<FName>; switch case 2 selects it; otherwise it is hidden before the selected array is shown. CP_050_00 and CP_050_20 reuse names between P2 and P3. Because all hidden entries precede the single shown entry, a shared name ends in the shown state when the selected pattern includes it.

MaterialName_P4.technical: TArray<FName>; switch case 3 selects it; otherwise it is hidden by the same pass. In the export only the seven CP_130_* rows populate P4 (three or four names each); every other row has six 'None' entries.

MaterialName_P5.technical: TArray<FName>; switch case 4 selects it; otherwise it is hidden. As with P4, only the seven CP_130_* rows have non-None entries in this export.

MaterialName_P6.technical: TArray<FName>; switch case 5 selects it; otherwise it is hidden. Only the seven CP_130_* rows have non-None entries in this export.

MaterialName_P7.technical: TArray<FName>; switch case 6 selects it; otherwise it is hidden. Only the seven CP_130_* rows have non-None entries in this export.

MaterialName_P8.technical: TArray<FName>; switch case 7 selects it; otherwise it is hidden. All six entries are 'None' in every one of the 27 exported rows, so pattern 7 is accepted and records AppliedPattern=7 but toggles no material sections in this export.

notes: The canonical export has 27 rows, each with ID and exactly MaterialName_P1 through MaterialName_P8; every array has six exported slots. P1 is populated in all rows, P2 in 19, P3 in 10, P4-P7 only in the seven CP_130_* rows, and P8 in none. The ten per-character export views are value-identical subsets of these rows, not additional runtime shards.

Pattern is a zero-based selector with no physical unit: 0..7 map to P1..P8. An out-of-range value returns before any section call or AppliedPattern write, leaving the previous value in place (0 on a fresh controller); AGameCharacter nevertheless forwards the raw value to ActionController::OnMaterialPatternChanged. The studio level-sequencer debug path uses -1 as a no-material-change value, while cinematic sequencer tracks clamp their evaluated value to 0..7.

Variations with Id_CharacterMaterial=None (335 of 437 exported variation rows) and lookups of a missing ID return before any section work. Of the 27 material row IDs, 26 are referenced by at least one variation and CP_110_20 is unreferenced; no exported variation points to a missing material row.

Material names are exact FName keys against the parent-material names harvested by Initialize into OutlineRimParameters. ShowMaterialSections acts only when the mesh is a USkinnedMeshComponent, changes every LOD, and marks the render state dirty; unmatched names are silently ignored.

Each successfully applied call processes hidden arrays first and the selected array last, so a name shared between patterns (for example between CP_050_00's P2 and P3) finishes shown when the selected array contains it. Array order itself is not a material-slot index; the harvested map supplies the material index.

AGameCharacter's interface call passes a null row and then notifies the action controller: CP_110 mirrors the pattern to its shikigami, and CP_150 uses pattern 1 to restore a passive buff. Animation notifies save/restore the value through GetMaterialPattern and a per-object cache, and sequencer evaluation saves AppliedPattern and restores it on teardown. These indirect consumers never read the arrays directly.

Shikigami material calls use UGameShikigamiMaterialController, FGameDataTableRow_ShikigamiMaterial (P1..P5 only) and ShikigamiMaterialDataTables at DTM +0x6D0; they are not consumers of CharacterMaterialDataTable.

Only one canonical asset plus per-character subset views are present in the export; no locale or numbered runtime shards were found. Retail Blueprint assets and loaded/cooked DataTable objects were not available here, so no Blueprint-only consumer or asset-existence claim is made.

usages.detail: Registers the unsharded name CharacterMaterialDataTable among the DataTable primary assets loaded by StartInitialLoading.
Once all loads complete, Tick resolves that loader to a UDataTable and appends it to CharacterMaterialDataTables (DTM +0x490); null results are skipped.
With a null row, resolves the current CharacterVariation through the cached character row and variation index.
Finds this material row by Variation.Id_CharacterMaterial in the manager's table list; first match wins.
Sorts the P1-P8 entries so hidden arrays are applied before the selected array, then toggles exact-name matches and stores AppliedPattern.
IGameActorInterface::SetMaterialPattern calls the controller with a null row and forwards the requested pattern to OnMaterialPatternChanged.
Battle spawn setup passes Slot.MaterialPattern directly to the character material controller.
Capture setup uses VariationParameter.MaterialPattern for SituationOverview captures and Slot.Parameter.MaterialPattern otherwise.
Animation notify caches the owner's current pattern by object index, switches to the notify pattern, and restores the cached value on end.
Cinematic tracks clamp the evaluated pattern to 0..7, save AppliedPattern once, and restore it on teardown when bResetParameter is set.
Indirect consumer: pattern 1 reapplies BUFF_CP_150_PASSIVE while the owner is alive.
Distinguishes the shikigami twin: its null-row lookup uses ShikigamiMaterialDataTables and only P1..P5.
